title: ALMA Observations of Magnetic Fields in the Massive Star-forming Region IRAS 18360-0537
question: Reveal the magnetic field structure at high angular resolutions and investigate the importance of the magnetic field, gravity, and turbulence in the formation of high-mass stars in IRAS18360-0537.

recipe.goal: Compute debiased polarized intensity, polarization fraction, and magnetic field position angles
recipe.method: Compute polarized intensity from quadrature sum of Stokes Q and U, debias following Vaillancourt (2006), apply 3 sigma_P cutoff, compute polarization percentage p = P/I and position angle, and rotate by 90 degrees to get magnetic field orientation.

Fit analytical hourglass models (parabolic model of Girart et al. 2006 and Green's function model of Ewertowski & Basu 2013) by minimizing chi^2 of position angle residuals, and independently apply the structure function method (Falceta-Goncalves et al. 2008; Hildebrand et al. 2009) and angle dispersion function (ADF; Houde et al. 2016).
key_parameters: Pixel size = 0.15'', angle measurement uncertainty sigma_phi = 1.4 deg; structure function fit range 1.1'' < l < 2.2''
assumptions: B0 = 1 in Ewertowski & Basu (2013) model; only first three terms in series considered; symmetry center and axis fixed to parabolic fit values

recipe.goal: Estimate gas temperature, mass, and volume density
recipe.method: Derive upper temperature limit via rotational diagram method on six unblended CH3OH lines; derive lower temperature limit by fitting VLA NH3 (1,1) and (2,2) hyperfine structure in GILDAS/CLASS; calculate gas mass and H2 volume density from 1.3 mm dust continuum and SMA mass.
key_parameters: Detected magnetic field region = 2.5'' x 1.95''; 3 sigma flux threshold for CH3OH transitions
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission, gas-to-dust ratio Lambda = 100, dust opacity kappa_nu = 2.9 cm^2 g^-1 with beta = 0.82, distance D = 6.3 kpc, LTE and optically thin CH3OH lines, line of sight axis aligned with minor axis of elliptical region, mean molecular weight mu = 2.86

recipe.method: Measure CH3OH(10_2,9-9_3,9) linewidth, deduct bulk motions from centroid velocity dispersion following Yue et al. (2021), and use RADMC-3D envelope-disk radiative transfer model from Mo & Qiu (2023) to remove infall and rotational bulk motions.
key_parameters: Protostar mass = 60 M_sun, envelope mass = 80 M_sun, inner radius r0 = 730 AU, outer radius R = 12600 AU, density profile rho prop r^-2.5

recipe.goal: Estimate magnetic field strength, mass-to-flux ratio, and B-field-to-gravity force ratio
recipe.method: Calculate plane-of-sky magnetic field strength B_pos via DCF equation (Crutcher et al. 2004), compute normalized mass-to-flux ratio lambda_obs and turbulent-to-magnetic energy ratio beta_turb, and apply the polarization-intensity gradient technique (Koch et al. 2012) to map Sigma_B = F_B / F_G.
key_parameters: Q = 0.28, n(H2) = 1.0 x 10^6 cm^-3, delta_v_turb = 1.4 km s^-1, geometric correction factor f = 3/4
assumptions: Equipartition of turbulent kinetic and magnetic energy for DCF (noted as likely violated, making B_pos an upper limit); oblately compressed spheroid core geometry (f = 3/4).

recipe.goal: Quantitatively compare magnetic field with outflow, rotation, and accretion kinematics
recipe.method: Estimate outflow kinetic energy from SiO dynamics using two outflow mass estimates; calculate rotational-to-magnetic energy ratio beta_r-B, angular-velocity-to-B criterion omega/B, and rotational-to-gravitational energy ratio beta_r-G; perform centroid velocity fitting on CH3OH(10_2,9-9_3,9) to derive enclosed mass; model accretion flow velocity between MM2 and MM1.
key_parameters: B_pos,u = 1.7 mG; M_out = 54 M_sun and 10 M_sun; v_rot = 2.4 km s^-1; V_A = 2.5 km s^-1; density power-law index n = 0 and 1.5; pseudo-disk radius R ~ 2500 AU; bandpass phase noise Phi_BP approx 3 deg; cylinder length 2L = 9500 AU; M1 = 10 M_sun
assumptions: Solid-body rotation and spherical moment of inertia for energy ratios; transitions localized on a fixed-radius disk (R ~ 2500 AU) for centroid velocity slope; cylindrical accretion flow between MM2 and MM1

score_reason: The ALMA project code, calibrators, imaging weighting, beam sizes, sensitivities, and mathematical equations for all post-processing steps (debiasing, hourglass model fitting, structure function, rotational diagram, DCF, and kinematic models) are clearly specified. However, key dependencies (VLA NH3 data, SMA masses, and RADMC-3D modeling in Mo & Qiu 2023) are external, and low-level CASA self-calibration and continuum subtraction parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA Cycle 5 dataset (2017.1.00793.S) is public in the archive, the continuum polarization debiasing, hourglass model fitting, structure function analysis, CH3OH rotational diagram, and CH3OH centroid velocity fitting follow standard, explicitly written equations, and the paper reports concrete numeric targets for all of them.
